reviewStatus: Drafted from primary sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Modified Rankin Scale

version.label: Modified Rankin Scale 0–6
version.detail: Rankin 1957, modified by van Swieten et al. 1988; grade 6 (death) as used in trials.

purpose: Global measure of disability and dependence in daily activities.
intendedPopulation: Adults after stroke and other neurological disorders.

inputDefinitions.label: Functional level
inputDefinitions.help: Choose the single level that best describes the patient's current overall function.

options.label: No significant disability
options.detail: Able to carry out all usual duties and activities despite some symptoms.

options.label: Slight disability
options.detail: Unable to do all previous activities, but looks after own affairs without help.

options.label: Moderate disability
options.detail: Needs some help, but walks without assistance.

options.label: Moderately severe disability
options.detail: Unable to walk or attend to bodily needs without assistance.

options.label: Severe disability
options.detail: Bedridden, incontinent, needs constant nursing care.

resultStates.label: No significant disability
resultStates.summary: Symptoms present; all usual activities possible.

resultStates.label: Slight disability
resultStates.summary: Independent in own affairs with some activity restriction.

resultStates.label: Moderate disability
resultStates.summary: Needs some help; walks without assistance.

resultStates.label: Moderately severe disability
resultStates.summary: Dependent for walking and bodily needs.

clinicalInsights.text: 'Favourable outcome' cut-offs differ between studies (0–1, 0–2, or ordinal shift). State the definition when comparing.
Boundaries between grades 1–3 have the most inter-rater variability; structured interviews improve reliability.

limitations: Moderate inter-rater reliability without a structured assessment.
Weighted toward mobility; cognition and mood may be under-represented.
commonErrors: Assigning 0 when minor symptoms persist (should be 1).

guideSections.what: A 7-level ordinal scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (dead) describing global disability.
guideSections.whenUseful: Stroke outcome assessment, documenting pre-morbid function, and follow-up.
guideSections.howToCalculate: Select the one level that best describes current function across all activities. Use a structured interview where possible.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Pre-stroke mRS is used in many protocols and should be documented with its source.

sources.citation: van Swieten JC, Koudstaal PJ, Visser MC, Schouten HJ, van Gijn J. Interobserver agreement for the assessment of handicap in stroke patients. Stroke. 1988;19(5):604-607.
Rankin J. Cerebral vascular accidents in patients over the age of 60. II. Prognosis. Scott Med J. 1957;2(5):200-215.

licensing.status: Widely published grade definitions, original wording
licensing.note: Structured mRS interview instruments (e.g. mRS-9Q, RFA) have their own terms and are not reproduced.
